dimensions.assessment: Affects federal rulemaking agencies, the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs, and public and private entities subject to major rules.
dimensions.evidence: Before promulgating any proposed or final major rule, the agency promulgating the major rule shall prepare and publish

dimensions.assessment: Imposes substantial procedural requirements on agencies promulgating major rules, including mandatory initial and final analyses and judicial review.
dimensions.evidence: A person that is aggrieved by final agency action in adopting a major rule that is subject to section 202 is entitled to judicial review

dimensions.assessment: Defines major rules based on an annual effect on the economy of $100,000,000 or more, adjusted for inflation.
dimensions.evidence: an annual effect on the economy of $100,000,000 or more, adjusted once every 5 years

dimensions.assessment: Amends statutory requirements across multiple federal acts regarding regulatory analysis, stakeholder consultations, and judicial review.
dimensions.evidence: The Unfunded Mandates Reform Act of 1995 (2 U.S.C. 1501 et seq.) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent statutory changes to federal agency rulemaking procedures.

missing_information: Exact figures on federal administrative costs to implement the new analyses.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill amends the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act of 1995 to impose new regulatory impact analysis and stakeholder consultation requirements on federal agencies for major rules, affecting federal agencies, the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs, and entities subject to major regulations.
